t: Above or below the pectinate line?
key: Ask which germ layer built that part of the canal: hindgut endoderm above the line brings visceral nerves and portal drainage, and ectoderm below brings somatic pain, caval veins and groin nodes.
items: They arise from the superior rectal venous plexus above the line, where visceral nerves make them painless.
Visceral afferents above the line sense stretch but not cutting or tearing, so lesions there bleed without pain.
The upper canal is lined by columnar epithelium of hindgut origin, the cell type of adenocarcinoma.
Endoderm of the hindgut forms the upper canal, so its lining matches the rectum above.
Superior rectal artery from the inferior mesenteric artery
The hindgut artery continues down to the line as the superior rectal artery.
Venous drainage to the portal system
The superior rectal vein drains to the inferior mesenteric vein and then to the portal vein.
Lymph above the line follows the rectal vessels to internal iliac nodes, not to the groin.
They arise from the inferior rectal plexus below the line under somatically innervated skin, so they hurt.
Stratified squamous lining from ectoderm gives rise to squamous cancers, often linked to HPV.
Inferior rectal nerve carries the pain
This somatic branch of the pudendal nerve supplies the canal below the line and the perianal skin.
A tear in the sensitive squamous lining below the line, usually posterior midline, causes sharp pain with stool.
Venous drainage to the caval system
Inferior rectal veins drain to the internal pudendal and internal iliac veins and then to the inferior vena cava.
Like the perineal skin around it, the lower canal drains to the groin nodes.
